sections.overview: Polyamide 612 is a long-chain aliphatic nylon designated by 6-carbon diamine and 12-carbon diacid-derived components. Its long aliphatic content differentiates it from shorter-chain nylon grades.
sections.history: PA612 was an established commercial nylon by the 1970s. A dated application milestone is the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s July 1975 action on a DuPont petition covering nylon 612 in repeated-use food-contact articles. DuPont also pursued flexible-tubing applications: Rolando Pagilagan’s 1978 patent describes modified 612-based copolyamides intended to improve resistance to zinc chloride. Together these records show the material’s role in manufactured articles and chemically demanding service, and the importance of formulation research after commercialization. Neither record establishes its first laboratory synthesis; the 1975 decision is historical evidence rather than a statement of present regulatory suitability.
sections.nomenclature: PA612 and nylon 612 name polyamide 612. The number pair specifies the polyamide structure and should not be treated as a generic label for all nylon composites or elastomers.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 612 (nylon 6,12) is the condensation polyamide from hexamethylenediamine and dodecanedioic acid. A practical salt route prepares aqueous diamine/diacid salt, concentrates it, then uses pressurised melt polymerisation with controlled steam release; subsequent finishing can raise molecular mass. Diamine:diacid stoichiometry and removal of condensation water control end-group balance and chain length. PA 612 is not synonymous with PA 612/6T or another copolyamide: incorporation of terephthalic acid, another lactam, or a different acid adds repeat units even where a PA 612 segment remains present.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 612 (PA612) is a semicrystalline long-chain aliphatic nylon used in unfilled, impact-modified, and fiber-filled compounds. Its stiffness, yield and break behavior depend on moisture or solvent uptake, molar mass, crystallinity/thermal history, glass-fiber content and orientation, impact modifier, molding direction, and temperature/rate. PA612 absorbs less water than PA6 or PA66, but polar liquids can plasticize it and lower strength; acid exposure can reduce molar mass and embrittle the polymer. A bounded commercial stock-shape example lists PA612 natural at 73 °F with ASTM D638 tensile strength at yield of 10,000 psi (about 69 MPa); it is a supplier’s unfilled grade value, not a general PA612 or reinforced-compound value.
sections.processing: PA612 is a relatively low-moisture-uptake thermoplastic used in injection molding, extrusion, tubing, and other semifinished forms; processing still depends on plasticizer, reinforcement, viscosity, and moisture history. Evonik's VESTAMID guide identifies PA612 molding compounds for extrusion and injection molding and gives PA612-specific dry-air drying at 80–110 °C for 2–4 h, with a plasticized PA612 melt range of 230–270 °C and mold range of 60–100 °C. The same guide warns that opened or damaged packaging can lead to moisture, bubbles, discoloration, and poor molding, and that exact settings depend on extrudate and machine. An independent PA612 two-component-bonding thesis describes injection molding PA612 thermoplastic inserts before transfer molding a rubber overmold; this confirms a bounded insert/overmolding route, but its process chain and material formulation should not be treated as a universal PA612 schedule.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA612 is a long-chain semicrystalline aliphatic nylon.
sections.properties: Water plasticization and compound formulation affect final mechanical behavior.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA612 is used in toothbrush bristles, abrasive filaments and filter fabrics, and in technical automotive components exposed to heat and fluids. Evonik identifies specialty PA612 grades for plastic–rubber composites.

Purchasing. Order a named PA612 resin/compound with the viscosity and additive package suited to bristle extrusion or component molding. Evonik’s VESTAMID D range and technical-sales channel provide documented commercial options.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable separate annual PA612 purchased or consumed tonnage was established from the checked manufacturer sources. Filament applications and grade ranges do not disclose a standard shipment mass or overall market volume.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: The supplier processing guide identifies degradation risks under excessive melt pressure; it does not quantify a PA612-specific product mixture.

Timescales: No PA612 environmental degradation duration is established by the processing guidance.

Environmental persistence: Environmental mineralization and persistence remain unquantified here. Processing failure cannot be substituted for those endpoints.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: The Evonik guide covering PA12 and PA612 documents regrind processing with appropriate melt filtration and controlled pressure. Acid recovery is additionally proposed for PA612 in a patent scope list, without a worked PA612 example.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 612 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: The cited VESTAMID source covers named compound systems.

sections.overview: Polyamide 11 is a long-chain aliphatic nylon made from 11-aminoundecanoic-acid-derived units. It is a distinct polyamide material often associated with bio-based feedstock routes.
sections.history: The PA11 commercial lineage began with Organico’s 1947 patent and the 1949 market launch of Rilsan. Production at Serquigny established a castor-oil-derived engineering polymer whose early applications included fuel lines in the Citroën DS in the 1950s. Later expansion included a U.S. plant at Birdsboro in 1970 and growth in automotive and oil-and-gas applications during the 1980s and 1990s. Arkema’s retrospective also traces subsequent use in sports equipment, composites and additive-manufacturing powders. The history is therefore both a long-running renewable-feedstock story and a progression from tubing to increasingly specialized products.
sections.nomenclature: PA11 and nylon 11 are standard names for polyamide 11. The designation specifies the 11-carbon amino-acid-derived repeat unit and is distinct from PA12 and other nylons.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 11 (PA11, polyundecanamide) is made by polycondensing 11-aminoundecanoic acid to form the C11 amide repeat unit. A laboratory-scale patent example polymerizes the amino acid under nitrogen with phosphoric acid as a catalyst or control additive; its mineral-filled composition is an example rather than the definition of neat PA11. A documented precursor route starts from castor oil, converts it through methyl ricinoleate and methyl 10-undecenoate to 10-undecenoic acid, then uses hydrobromination and ammonolysis to obtain 11-aminoundecanoic acid. That origin is route-specific, so the PA11 name alone does not guarantee a particular renewable content.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 11 (PA11) is a semicrystalline long-chain aliphatic polyamide that can combine yielding with substantial post-yield drawing, but its stiffness, strength, and break strain vary with grade, molecular mass, crystallinity and crystal morphology, moisture, temperature and strain rate, pigment or reinforcement, and the molding, extrusion, or powder-bed route. Cooling history is consequential: in rotationally molded PA11 liner specimens, faster cooling lowered crystallinity, tensile/flexural strength and modulus while increasing elongation. A tightly bounded unfilled example is heat- and light-stabilized Arkema Rilsan BESNO TL extrusion-grade PA11: compression-molded 4 mm-gauge-thickness dumbbells tested on an Instron at 5 mm/min gave 930 ± 40 MPa Young modulus, 29 ± 1 MPa yield stress, 52 ± 3 MPa stress at break, and 300 ± 20% strain at break (seven-specimen averages). Pellets were dried before melt mixing, but test temperature and specimen conditioning are not reported; these values therefore describe that compression-molded grade and test, not PA11 generally. The hot-pressed PA11 comparison likewise shows that pressing route and resulting crystallinity can produce a much lower-elongation response, reinforcing that PA11 film, tube, liner, and molded-grade results are not interchangeable.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 11 (PA11) is available across viscosities for injection molding; cast- and blown-film, sheet, tube, profile, and blow-molding extrusion; coextrusion and overmolding; rotational molding; and additive manufacture by powder-bed fusion or material extrusion. Moisture control is central even though PA11 absorbs less water than shorter-chain nylons: keep packages closed, prevent condensation, and dry exposed granules without oxidizing them. In extrusion, screw design, feed cooling, melt homogeneity, die temperature, draw-down, vacuum sizing, circulating-water calibration, and controlled cooling set wall thickness and surface quality. In molding and powder-bed fusion, mold or bed temperature and cooling rate govern crystallization, shrinkage, warpage, and residual stress; prolonged oxygen exposure at heat promotes degradation.

Arkema's guidance is explicitly for Rilsan PA11 grades. It directs drying after more than two hours of atmospheric exposure for 4–8 h at 80–90 °C, gives hopper/feed/compression/metering/head/die settings of 60/175/220/235/230/220 °C for BESNO P40 TL and 60/180/225/240/230/220 °C for BESNO P20 TL, and requires below 0.1% moisture for film and pipe extrusion. Its tube guidance uses 50–400 mbar vacuum calibration, while its PA11 rotomolding grades are heated to 260–300 °C and preferably cooled air–water–air to limit distortion and thermal shock. As a distinct powder-bed example, Colucci and co-workers processed Wematter Aurora PA11 in nitrogen at an approximately 187 °C bed temperature, with 27 W laser power, 0.1 mm layers, 100 warming layers, and a 170–190 °C experiment-defined sintering window. Those values are grade-, powder-, machine-, and article-specific.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA11 is a long-chain semicrystalline nylon with an 11-carbon repeat-unit origin.
sections.properties: Crystallinity, moisture, and cooling rate govern mechanics and barrier behavior.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA11 is used in automotive fuel-management systems, tubing and hoses, medical devices and catheters, sporting goods and powder-bed-fusion printing. These uses span transportation, medical technology, energy and consumer products.

Purchasing. Buy a qualified molding/extrusion resin or an application-specific powder. Arkema’s Rilsan KNO data sheet explicitly identifies PA11 pellets for injection molding; its material database and contact channel support grade selection.

Scale and evidence limits. Arkema describes its Singapore investment as increasing global PA11 capacity by 50%. That is a relative capacity change, without an absolute annual tonnage in the checked page, and is not a purchase or output statistic. A reliable separate consumption total was not established.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Hydrochloric-acid cleavage produces 11-aminoundecanoic acid hydrochloride.

Timescales: Unfilled PA11 pellets required 40 min at 200 °C with HCl/amide ratio 1.25 for complete conversion in the microwave study.

Environmental persistence: The cited chemical-recovery experiments do not measure environmental mineralization. No soil, freshwater or marine disappearance time is established here.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: Acid depolymerization recovers amino-acid feedstock. A separate repeated-melt-processing study demonstrates recycling of specified PA11/basalt-fiber/flame-retardant formulations, with properties and fire behavior checked after processing; bio-based origin alone does not establish biodegradability.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 11 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: Rotomolded and blend results are process- and formulation-specific.

sections.overview: Polyamide 12 is a long-chain aliphatic nylon commonly made by ring-opening polymerization of laurolactam. Its relatively long methylene sequence differentiates it from shorter-chain nylons.
sections.history: Chemische Werke Hüls presented pilot-scale VESTAMID PA12 at the K’63 trade fair in 1963 and began production at Marl in 1964. A larger reactor followed in 1966, helping supply automotive plastic components. This commercial lineage later became part of Evonik. The company’s retrospective traces PA12 from these early engineering uses into a wider portfolio, while recent work has addressed alternative feedstocks and the environmental burden of production. Those newer production options preserve the PA12 chemical identity. The Hüls dates identify a documented pilot-to-production sequence rather than proof that no earlier laboratory PA12 existed.
sections.nomenclature: PA12 and nylon 12 name polyamide 12. The designation is a specific polymer identity and should not be used as a generic name for long-chain polyamides.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 12 (PA12, polydodecanamide) is prepared from 12-aminododecanoic acid by polycondensation or from laurolactam by water-assisted ring opening followed by condensation. These are alternative routes to the C12 amide repeat unit when no comonomer is incorporated. A disclosed lactam process combines initial ring opening/prepolymer formation with melt condensation at ordinary or reduced pressure. A reported industrial precursor sequence makes laurolactam through cyclododecane/cyclododecanone/oxime chemistry; that is one feedstock route rather than an intrinsic PA12 identity claim.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 12 (PA12) is a semicrystalline long-chain aliphatic polyamide often selected where a comparatively moisture-tolerant, tough, ductile engineering thermoplastic is needed. Its tensile response nevertheless depends on molecular mass and grade, crystallinity and crystal phase, additive or reinforcement package, moisture uptake, temperature and loading rate, and whether the material is injection molded, hot pressed, extruded as tubing, or built from powder. In medical PA12 testing, increased temperature and water conditioning both softened the material, and necked tubes had lower modulus and yield stress than standardized dogbones; geometry and forming history therefore cannot be ignored. At 23 °C, dogbone specimens of the study's unspecified medical PA12 stored at ambient temperature/humidity and pulled at 50 mm/min had a median Young modulus of 1,553.49 MPa (IQR 233.1 MPa) and yield stress of 45.53 MPa (IQR 0.4 MPa). The report does not identify a commercial grade or the exact ambient conditioning, so these are material-and-test-specific values, not PA12 family constants. Independent hot-pressed commercial PA12 sheet data show how processing and crystallinity can change the balance: ASTM D638 specimens at 0.5 mm/min gave 2,964.3 ± 102.8 MPa modulus, 64.0 ± 3.2 MPa ultimate strength, and 200% elongation at break; grade and post-press conditioning were not reported.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 12 (PA12) is processed by injection molding; extrusion of tube, pipe, film, coating, wire and cable jacket, and filament; blow molding for suitable grades; and additive manufacture by laser sintering, high-speed or multi-jet powder fusion, and fused-filament deposition. Keep pellets dry and prevent cross-contamination, because excess moisture causes bubbles and molding defects while incompatible polymers weaken weld lines. For extrusion, match the screw and heat profile to grade and geometry, cool the feed zone, monitor actual melt temperature rather than heater settings alone, and coordinate die draw-down with vacuum sizing, water-film pre-quench, puller speed, and final cooling. Powder age, oxygen level, time near melting, repeated shear, crystallization history, and cooling rate change melt flow, shrinkage, warpage, porosity, and layer bonding.

Evonik's VESTAMID guide gives supplier-specific PA12 practice: unopened material is normally used as supplied, whereas damaged or long-open packages are dried to below 0.1% water, typically 2–4 h at 80–100 °C in dehumidified air. It lists grade-specific melt intervals rather than one PA12 number—for example 190–230 °C for L1600, 180–220 °C for L1670, and 240–280 °C for L-GF30—and recommends PA12 mold temperatures of 30–100 °C. Feng, Wang, and Wei give a distinct recycled-powder example: recycled SLS PA12 was dried at 60 °C for 3 h and twin-screw granulated through 225/240/255/260/260/240 °C zones; fresh and recycled pellets were filament-extruded after drying with 210/240/220/50 °C zones, then printed at 235 °C nozzle, 110 °C bed, 0.1 mm layer, and 40 mm/s. The authors also observed that friction made actual compounding temperature exceed settings and that oxygen plus heat and shear promoted oxidative chain scission, so these values are not a universal PA12 window.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA12 is a long-chain semicrystalline nylon often made from laurolactam.
sections.properties: Mechanical and durability response depend on moisture, thermal history, and specimen form.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA12 is used in automotive fluid and air lines, oil-and-gas pipes, wire/cable coverings, medical catheters and precision parts. PA12 powders also serve industrial additive manufacturing.

Purchasing. Order a specified PA12 compound for extrusion or molding, or a powder qualified for the printing process. Evonik separates VESTAMID L engineering materials from INFINAM PA12 printing powders and provides product and technical contacts.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable separate annual purchased or consumed PA12 tonnage was established from the checked manufacturer pages. Powder grades and engineering compounds represent different commercial forms and cannot be assigned the same order size.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Hydrochloric-acid cleavage yields 12-aminododecanoic acid hydrochloride.

Timescales: PA12 pellets reached complete conversion at 200 °C in 10 min with HCl/amide ratio 2.5 in the microwave study.

Environmental persistence: The cited chemical-recovery experiments do not measure environmental mineralization. No soil, freshwater or marine disappearance time is established here.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: Monomer recovery by acid hydrolysis is demonstrated. Separately, used selective-laser-sintering PA12 powder was extruded into filament for fused-deposition printing, providing a polymer-reuse route for that powder stream rather than proof that indefinitely aged powder remains suitable.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 12 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: Balloon-catheter and hot-pressed-sheet data are not general PA12 values.

synthesisRoutes.mechanism: Water-assisted lactam opening and condensation form PA12. In the water-assisted route, lactam opening generates amino/carboxyl functionality. Amino ends add further lactam through ring-opening acyl substitution, while amino and carboxyl ends also undergo condensation. The balance of ring opening, condensation and water-dependent equilibria controls polymer and residual cyclic species.

sections.overview: Polyamide 1010 is an aliphatic nylon whose designation reflects its diamine and diacid carbon counts. It is a distinct long-chain polyamide used in molded and film materials.
sections.history: PA1010 has a distinct long-chain-polyamide history and should not inherit nylon 66’s invention date. A documented later development is Evonik’s March 2010 introduction of VESTAMID Terra DS compounds for high-performance cable jackets. The announcement identifies PA1010 made from castor-oil-derived monomers and targets automotive cables, buried cables and polymer optical fibers. This shows how renewable monomer supply and compound development expanded an established polymer chemistry into specialized electrical applications. The 2010 date describes that product expansion, not the first synthesis of PA1010; the available historical evidence here does not establish a single original inventor.
sections.nomenclature: PA1010 and nylon 1010 name polyamide 1010. The numeric designation specifies its monomer-derived polyamide structure and is not interchangeable with other nylon-number grades.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 1010 (PA1010, polydecamethylene sebacamide) is the aliphatic condensation polyamide from 1,10-decanediamine and sebacic acid. The 10/10 designation identifies those monomer chain lengths. The pair may first be made into an approximately equimolar nylon salt, then melt-polycondensed while condensate is removed; solution and solid-state polymerization are documented alternatives. Biomass-origin claims are feedstock-route specific, not intrinsic to the PA1010 name.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 1010 (PA1010) is a semicrystalline long-chain polyamide, so mechanical comparisons need to retain crystallization/thermal history, moisture conditioning, specimen form and orientation, temperature, and any reinforcement or crosslinking treatment. A room-temperature cast-extruded PA1010 film study reported a tensile modulus of 762.1 ± 57.5 MPa, yield stress of 45.4 ± 3.3 MPa, and elongation at break of 155.06 ± 36.3%. In a separate gamma-irradiation study, unmodified PA1010 had tensile strength 40 ± 1.2 MPa, modulus 1.4 ± 0.06 GPa, and elongation at break 121 ± 5%; irradiation and triallyl isocyanurate formulation changed the response. The film and irradiated-specimen values are bounded examples, not a universal PA1010 specification.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 1010 (PA1010) can be melt compounded and pelletized, injection molded into engineering parts, and extruded into tube, profile, sheet, or cast film. Conversion follows long-chain-polyamide practice: keep pellets or powder dry and protected from ambient moisture, feed uniformly, limit hot residence and oxygen exposure, and match screw shear and melt temperature to molecular weight, fillers, and article geometry. Film gauge depends on die uniformity, screw output, chill-roll temperature and speed, draw-down, and calender or take-off balance; injection filling and crystallization depend on melt homogeneity, gate and venting, mold temperature, packing, and cooling. Regrind and filled formulations require renewed drying and attention to contamination and viscosity drift.

Two open experiments show distinct routes without defining a universal PA1010 window. Hernández-García and co-workers dried their synthesized PA1010 powder, then produced about 145 µm cast film on a 20 mm, 25 L/D single-screw extruder with a 120 mm flat die and three-roll chill/calender unit; the set profile was 35 °C at feed, then 210–210–210–210–230 °C at the head, with the screw at 30 rpm, and film thickness was adjusted through calender and drag speed. Morino and co-workers instead dry-blended Vestamid Terra DS16 PA1010 with or without the stated TAIC additive, vacuum-dried at 80 °C for 12 h, twin-screw mixed at 220 °C and 85 rpm, strand-pelletized, dried again, and injection molded at 220 °C nozzle and cylinder, 40 °C mold, and 13 cm3/s. Those conditions belong to the named powder, grade, formulations, and laboratory equipment.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA1010 is a semicrystalline long-chain aliphatic nylon.
sections.properties: Crystallinity, moisture, and processing influence its film and molded-material properties.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA1010 is commercially offered for mono- and multifilaments used by textile manufacturers. Evonik’s VESTAMID Terra DS1601 NC is a specific documented grade, with textile fibers and oral-care markets listed.

Purchasing. Purchase PA1010 base-polymer pellets or a tailored compound. DS1601 NC is supplied in moisture-proof polyethylene bags; specify the filament application and required grade through the manufacturer’s product-contact channel.

Scale and evidence limits. The checked source gives a packaging type but no package mass, minimum order or annual sales tonnage. No reliable separate purchased or consumed PA1010 volume was established.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Microwave-assisted acid hydrolysis yields sebacic acid and protonated 1,10-decanediamine.

Timescales: The tested PA1010 pellets reached complete conversion in 17 min at 200 °C and HCl/amide ratio 2.5.

Environmental persistence: The cited chemical-recovery experiments do not measure environmental mineralization. No soil, freshwater or marine disappearance time is established here.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: The laboratory process separates the diacid and diamine for feedstock recovery. This establishes chemical feasibility, not a commercial collection system for PA1010.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 1010 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: Cast-film results are tied to specified resin and extrusion conditions.

synthesisRoutes.mechanism: Diamine–diacid polycondensation forms PA1010. Amine and carboxyl groups form amide bonds with net elimination of water. Monofunctional species or an end-group imbalance limit the attainable chain length.

sections.overview: Polyamide 1012 is a long-chain aliphatic nylon designated by its 10-carbon diamine and 12-carbon diacid-derived components. It is a distinct engineering polyamide used in applications such as tubing and compounds.
sections.history: PA1012 was already among the long-chain polyamides considered for automotive multilayer tubing in Degussa research with 2000 priority, later granted as a 2004 patent to Hans Ries, Guido Schmitz and Harald Haeger. The work addressed adhesion between chemically different polyamide layers while retaining the outer layer’s resistance to service conditions. A later Evonik patent application published in 2011 included PA1012 powders for layerwise molding, documenting expansion toward additive manufacturing. These sources trace practical development in tubing and powder processing. They do not identify the first PA1012 synthesis or imply that these patent dates mark the polymer’s original invention.
sections.nomenclature: PA1012 and nylon 1012 are names for polyamide 1012. Its number pair distinguishes it from PA1010, PA12, and other aliphatic polyamide grades.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 1012 (PA1012, polydecamethylene dodecanediamide) is the long-chain aliphatic condensation polyamide from 1,10-decanediamine and dodecanedioic acid; the 10/12 designation identifies those monomer chain lengths. A documented aqueous route first reacts the monomers in a salt-forming vessel under inert gas, then transfers the charge to a pressurized polymerization vessel for high-temperature polycondensation and granulation. Another autoclave example combines the same monomer pair with water and a small amount of hypophosphorous acid. These are bounded process examples: antioxidants, nucleating agents, and phosphorus additives are route-specific, and bio-based provenance is not intrinsic to the PA1012 name.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 1012 (PA1012) is a semicrystalline long-chain polyamide; mechanical results must be tied to crystal form and thermal history, moisture state, molecular weight, specimen geometry/orientation, temperature, and any filler or blend. In a PA1012/multi-walled-carbon-nanotube automotive fuel-pipe study, the reported pipe at 20 °C had tensile strength 35.3 MPa and elongation at break 240%; at 90 °C those values were 23.4 MPa and 333%, while at −40 °C they were 59.3 MPa and 40%. A separate PA1012/calcium-sulfate-whisker study reported filler-dependent nucleation, rheological/storage-modulus changes, and a substantial flexural response while tensile strength changed little. The pipe values apply to that composite pipe and temperature series, not to neat PA1012 or other grades/forms.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 1012 (PA1012) is melt-processable by twin-screw compounding and pelletizing, injection molding, and single- or multilayer extrusion of tube and pipe; film, profile, and other engineering shapes are also plausible where an appropriate grade is supplied, but the cited evidence here directly establishes compounding, injection molding, and pipe extrusion. Pellets should be dried and kept closed before melt processing. Screw design, filler feeding and dispersion, shear history, melt temperature, residence time, die pressure, cooling/calibration, and take-off govern surface quality, dimensions, crystallization, and filler-network orientation. Repeated or aggressive processing can alter hydrogen bonding, crystallization, and molecular weight, so a temperature profile must be tied to grade and formulation rather than treated as a family constant.

Li and co-workers give a bounded pipe process for their PA1012/MWCNT formulation. They vacuum-dried the supplied PA1012 at 95 °C for 15 h, made a 15 wt% MWCNT masterbatch and diluted it by twin-screw extrusion at 180 rpm with an 11-position profile of 180/220/230/230/230/220/210/220/230/240/240 °C, then extruded 6 mm OD, 4 mm ID automotive tube on a 45 mm, 30 L/D single screw at 230 rpm with 180/230/240/240/230/220 °C zone-to-die settings. Larger 63 and 166 mm pipe examples used slower 55 and 90 mm screws, and the high-pressure construction added a steel-wire spiral and outer polyethylene layer. In a distinct formulation, Lu and co-workers vacuum-dried PA1012 pellets at 85 °C overnight, twin-screw compounded PA1012 with 5–30 wt% 3-pentadecylphenol over 210–220 °C at 30 rpm, and micro-injection molded specimens at 225 °C and 0.6 MPa. These settings are specific to the cited resin, fillers, and equipment.

sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA1012 is commercially represented by Evonik’s VESTAMID Terra DD. Its supplier’s Terra portfolio offers compounds for molded technical/consumer parts, filaments and extruded products; the brochure discusses these uses across several Terra chemistries rather than assigning their market shares specifically to PA1012.

Purchasing. PA1012 is offered as Terra DD base-polymer pellets, with tailored compound formulations available by inquiry. Specify the exact DD grade and intended application; PA610 and PA1010 products in the same brochure are different materials.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable PA1012-only purchased or consumed tonnage, standard pack mass or industry allocation was established. The supplier evidence establishes a commercial material and possible portfolio uses, not verified widespread adoption in every illustrated application.

sections.overview: Polyamide 6T is a semi-aromatic nylon containing hexamethylenediamine- and terephthalate-derived units. Its aromatic diacid component differentiates it from aliphatic PA6 and supports high-temperature engineering use.
sections.history: PA6T was part of mid-twentieth-century research on heat-resistant terephthalamide fibers. Eugene Magat’s DuPont patent, filed in 1952 and granted in 1956, treats straight-chain terephthalamides as known materials whose high melting temperatures hinder ordinary melt spinning. That processing difficulty helped motivate work on modified diamines and copolyamides. Later DuPont research, including Rolando Pagilagan’s 1978 patent, incorporated 6T units into long-chain polyamide compositions for tubing. These records show PA6T chemistry becoming a tool for designing specialized materials. They do not make the commercial introduction dates of modified copolyamides into invention dates for the PA6T homopolymer.
sections.nomenclature: PA6T abbreviates polyamide 6T. The “T” denotes terephthalate-derived units, so it is distinct from PA6 and from mixed semi-aromatic copolyamides containing 6T units.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 6T (PA6T) is the semiaromatic condensation polyamide from hexamethylenediamine and terephthalic acid. A common route first neutralizes near-equimolar diamine and diacid in water to form a 6T nylon salt, then concentrates and heats the salt under pressure while removing water to form prepolymer; melt or solid-state polycondensation can then raise molar mass. One cited example prepares an aqueous 6T salt with pH adjustment from hexamethylenediamine and terephthalic acid, while a separate patent identifies salt formation, prepolymerization, and optional melt, solution, or solid-phase finishing as the general sequence. Stoichiometric balance and water removal are molecular-mass controls. Copolyamides in which adipic acid, isophthalic acid, or another monomer is deliberately added are 6T-based copolymers rather than the PA6T homopolymer described here.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 6T (PA6T) is a semi-aromatic high-temperature polyamide; commercial moldable materials are often PA6T-containing copolyamides and may be heavily reinforced, so composition must remain attached to every property. Tensile and interlaminar response depend on aromatic/aliphatic comonomer ratio, moisture, molecular mass, crystallinity, glass- or carbon-fiber content and architecture/orientation, interface sizing, thermal ageing, molding or consolidation route, and temperature/rate. In an explicitly composite-only endpoint, a compression-molded carbon-fiber fabric/PA6T laminate containing 36.2 vol% fiber achieved 507.8 MPa tensile strength and 43.1 GPa tensile modulus after prePA6T sizing and in-situ polymerization; this is not a neat PA6T value. A separate PA6T/6I/66 GF30 injection-molding datasheet illustrates composition and conditioning sensitivity, listing dry/conditioned 23 °C ISO 527 tensile strengths of 190/170 MPa.
sections.processing: PA6T belongs to the high-temperature polyphthalamide family and is generally converted by injection molding or by melt processing in reinforced composite structures; exact windows depend strongly on copolymerization with other phthalamide units, reinforcement, and grade design. An open Amodel PPA processing guide recommends desiccant-hopper drying for hygroscopic PPA, conventional injection equipment, controlled mold temperature, and avoidance of extended residence above 350 °C because degradation can result; those are PPA-family guidelines rather than a homopolymer PA6T specification. A separate open PA6T composite study used ultrafine PA6T powder as an emulsion/sizing route and manufactured continuous carbon-fiber/PA6T composites by coating, impregnation, hot pressing, and powder/compression molding. The powder size and composite architecture are bounded to that experiment, while PA6T/6I/6T-X molding grades require their own drying, melt, and mold qualification.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA6T is a semi-aromatic nylon with terephthalate units.
sections.properties: Crystallinity, reinforcement, and thermal history control high-temperature behavior.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. The checked commercial examples are PA6T-containing copolyamides used for molded engineering and metal-replacement parts. They do not establish a comparable commodity market for neat PA6T homopolymer.

Purchasing. EMS lists Grivory HT1 as PA6T/6I and HT2 as PA6T/66, with reinforcement and functional variants. Specify copolyamide composition explicitly when purchasing a melt-processable PA6T-based compound.

Scale and evidence limits. No separate neat-PA6T purchase volume is established here. Sales of PA6T-containing copolyamides must not be reported as homopolymer tonnage.
sections.degradationAndStability:

Timescales: No material-specific conversion time is demonstrated in that patent; its worked examples use PA66.

sections.overview: Polyamide 9T is a semi-aromatic nylon containing 9-carbon diamine and terephthalate-derived units. The aromatic terephthalate component distinguishes it from aliphatic long-chain nylons.
sections.history: Kuraray commercialized its GENESTAR heat-resistant polyamide business in 1999 after developing the material’s distinctive monomer system. PA9T became associated especially with connectors for mobile phones and computers, followed by automotive gears, fuel-system and cooling-system parts. Kuraray’s 2012 report describes expansion beyond the original connector market and continued grade development. Its later product literature distinguishes PA9T from PA9C, including reflector-oriented materials, so not every GENESTAR application should be assigned to PA9T. The 1999 date is a commercial milestone in Kuraray’s PA9T lineage, rather than a date for the entire polyphthalamide family.
sections.nomenclature: PA9T abbreviates polyamide 9T. The “T” identifies terephthalate-derived units, and the name is distinct from PA10T and other semi-aromatic polyamides.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 9T (PA9T) is the semiaromatic condensation polyamide from 1,9-nonanediamine and terephthalic acid. The monomers may first be combined in water as a near-stoichiometric nylon 9T salt, after which pressurized melt polycondensation removes water and forms prepolymer; further pressure reduction, melt residence, or solid-state advancement can increase conversion. A continuous salt-preparation example meters aqueous nonanediamine into a terephthalic-acid dispersion while controlling pH. A separate polymerization patent charges nonanediamine, terephthalic acid, water, sodium hypophosphite, and benzoic acid under nitrogen and documents staged pressure/temperature reduction to a PA9T prepolymer. The catalyst/end-group regulator and exact stages are route-specific. PA9T copolymers containing other diamines or diacids should not be generalized to this homopolymer composition.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 9T (PA9T) is a semi-aromatic high-temperature polyamide whose response is strongly grade-dependent: moisture state, impact modification, glass- or carbon-fiber loading and orientation, crosslinking, molded geometry, thermal history, and test temperature/rate all change the measured stiffness, strength, and break strain. Commercial PA9T data span unreinforced and heavily reinforced formulations and must not be combined as a polymer-wide range. For a bounded unreinforced injection-molding grade, BADAMID PA9T S at 23 °C lists ISO 527 tensile modulus 2900 MPa at 1 mm min−1, tensile stress at break 85 MPa at 5 mm min−1, and break strain 4% in the dry-as-molded state. A separate PA9T compound comparison shows the reinforcement effect: PA9T GF30 was reported at 150 MPa tensile strength and 9500 MPa tensile modulus by ISO 527; this is a 30% glass-fiber grade, not neat PA9T.
sections.processing: PA9T is a high-temperature, low-moisture-uptake polyphthalamide normally converted by injection molding, including reinforced and flame-retardant grades. Kuraray's Genestar PA9T guide recommends drying to below 0.1% moisture, preferably at 120 °C for 5 h, with a preferred melt temperature of 310–345 °C, mold temperature above 140 °C, high injection speed, and pressure/back-pressure limits; these are starting values for Genestar grades and should be adjusted for mold design and wall thickness. An independent open injection study used a commercial PA9T grade with 90 °C/4 h drying, 295–325 °C barrel zones, 140 °C mold, 170 MPa injection pressure, 50 mm/s injection rate, 25 s cooling, and 15 s holding. Its grade, crosslinking formulation, and test-bar geometry make the schedule a bounded experiment rather than a family-wide PA9T specification.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA9T is a semi-aromatic, terephthalate-containing nylon.
sections.properties: Properties depend on crystallinity, reinforcement, and grade formulation.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA9T serves electrical/electronic and automotive components where heat resistance and dimensional stability are useful. GENESTAR is one supplier’s PA9T product range.

Purchasing. Kuraray provides the GENESTAR range through product and technical-sales inquiries; select a grade and reinforcement package for the part. PA9T must not be substituted with a generic high-temperature nylon on the purchase specification.

Scale and evidence limits. Kuraray’s April 2023 announcement gives its new Rayong, Thailand, PA9T plant a capacity of 13,000 tonnes/year, an order of 10⁴ tonnes/year. This is nameplate capacity at one plant, not measured purchases or worldwide PA9T output.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: An acid-hydrolysis patent names PA9T in its scope, targeting diamine and diacid recovery. It does not establish this material’s major environmental degradation products.

sections.overview: Polyamide 10T is a semi-aromatic nylon formed from decanediamine- and terephthalate-derived units. Its terephthalate content differentiates it from aliphatic long-chain polyamides and supports high-temperature engineering applications.
sections.history: Unitika records development of XecoT heat-resistant polyamide in 2010. Its subsequent technical announcements identify the base material as PA10T, made using a biomass-derived monomer and developed for demanding molded components. In 2021, Unitika introduced reinforced XecoT grades intended to substitute for PA6T or PA66 during supply shortages, with automotive, electrical and sliding-part applications. This sequence shows PA10T advancing through polymer development and later compounding to meet manufacturing needs. The 2010 milestone is Unitika’s documented product development, not a claim that all PA10T chemistry originated that year.
sections.nomenclature: PA10T abbreviates polyamide 10T. The “T” denotes terephthalate-derived units, so the name should not be treated as a synonym for all PA10 grades.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 10T (PA10T, polydecamethylene terephthalamide) is the semi-aromatic condensation polyamide from 1,10-decanediamine and terephthalic acid. The 10 identifies the diamine chain and T the terephthalate unit. Disclosed routes form a nylon salt at close acid/diamine stoichiometry, then use melt polycondensation and, where needed, solid-phase polymerization. Water management and phosphorus-containing control additives are route-specific, not defining components of every PA10T.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 10T (PA10T) is a semicrystalline semi-aromatic polyamide whose terephthalamide units favor a stiff, high-strength, heat-capable response, while its longer decamethylene segment contributes chain flexibility and rapid crystallization. Mechanical behavior is especially sensitive to crystallinity and thermal history, moisture uptake and conditioning, molecular mass, impact-modifier or blend content, glass-fiber level and orientation, and injection-molding shrinkage/orientation. Glass-fiber-reinforced grades should not be used as evidence for neat PA10T: they are formulated for a much stiffer, lower-elongation response. In an unfilled PA10T comparison, dried extruded pellets were injection molded at a 150 °C mold temperature and tested at 10 mm/min by ISO 527: tensile strength was 70.3 MPa; the same study reports 132.3 MPa flexural strength, 2,670 MPa flexural modulus, 7.9 kJ/m² notched Izod impact strength, and 3.9% tensile strain at break. The source does not identify a commercial PA10T grade, test temperature, or post-molding conditioning, so these values are limited to its injection-molded unfilled research material. That study also found increasing PPO/SEBS-g-MAH blend content lowered strength/modulus while raising notched impact resistance, demonstrating a formulation-specific stiffness–toughness tradeoff. Independent PA10T technical material explains that glass-fiber reinforcement and high-temperature service applications further change the relevant compound and part response.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 10T (PA10T) and PA10T-rich copolyamides are high-melting, semicrystalline polyphthalamides processed chiefly by melt compounding and injection molding; commercial families also provide reinforced, flame-retarded, low-friction, and other molding grades. Extrusion of suitable compounds is possible, but the high melting point leaves less margin between melting and thermal degradation than for many aliphatic nylons. Feedstock therefore needs effective drying and protected handling, and processing should use a short, controlled hot residence, adequate venting, homogeneous but not excessive shear, and rapid purging after interruptions. Mold temperature and cooling control crystallization, shrinkage, surface quality, and dimensional stability, while filler feeding and screw configuration control fiber damage and dispersion.

EMS-GRIVORY identifies its Grivory HT3 base as PA10T/X and presents the family as economically injection moldable, with glass- and carbon-fiber, flame-retarded, and electro-compatible product variants; it does not establish a universal temperature schedule. Takenaka, Nishitani, and Kitano provide a bounded actual example for Vestamid HT plus M3000 PA10T and its 20 wt% PTFE and glass-fiber formulations. They vacuum-dried PA10T and glass fiber at 90 °C for 4 h, dry-blended the constituents, twin-screw melt-mixed at 310 °C and 85 rpm, cut approximately 5 mm pellets, dried again at 90 °C for 4 h, and injection molded with a 310 °C cylinder, 150 °C cavity, and 6 cm3/s injection rate. Those elevated values belong to that named resin and composite experiment, not every PA10T or PA10T copolyamide.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA10T is a semi-aromatic semicrystalline nylon containing terephthalate units.
sections.properties: High-temperature behavior depends on crystallinity, reinforcement, and blend formulation.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA10T-based commercial materials include LED reflector compounds and automotive components. Kingfa’s portfolio also describes broader semi-aromatic-polyamide uses; those broader claims do not establish that every application uses PA10T.

Purchasing. Specify a PA10T-based Vicnyl grade, reinforcement and any copolyamide content through Kingfa technical sales. The supplier’s HTPA umbrella includes several chemistries, so an HTPA designation alone is incomplete.

Scale and evidence limits. The checked supplier page provides no separate PA10T annual purchased or consumed mass. Neither the full HTPA portfolio nor LED-market revenue is a PA10T tonnage estimate.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: A patent examines ageing of a PA10T formulation containing epoxy-functional additive, ferric sulfate and antioxidant. It measures strength and melt-flow changes rather than identifying degradation molecules.

Timescales: The patent exposure is 1,000 h at 135 °C in equal proportions of ethylene glycol and water, with tensile testing of 4 mm specimens. This is accelerated coolant ageing of the stated formulation.

Environmental persistence: The accelerated test does not establish outdoor lifetime, biodegradation or mineralization of neat PA10T.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: A Kingfa patent gives a direct PA10T solvent-reclamation example. It dissolves PA10T waste in a phenol/toluene/methanol mixture at 80 °C, treats the solution with activated carbon, cools and filters it, then adds it to water to precipitate polymer for drying. This recovers polymer through dissolution and reprecipitation rather than recovering diamine and terephthalic acid. The evidence is a patent example; it does not establish a commercial collection system, solvent-recovery efficiency or universal applicability to all PA10T compounds.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 10T processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: PA10T/PPO blend data do not represent neat PA10T.

sections.overview: Poly(m-xylylene adipamide) is a semi-aromatic nylon formed from meta-xylylenediamine and adipic acid. Its aromatic diamine content differentiates it from aliphatic nylons and supports barrier-material applications.
sections.history: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical began producing MX-Nylon, its MXD6 polyamide, at Niigata in 1984. The company’s historical timeline records expansions in 1991 and 1997 and production in the United States in 2004. Its integrated business linked meta-xylylenediamine manufacture with polymer development. Food-packaging films and PET bottles became important markets because MXD6 could provide a gas-barrier component, while engineering-plastics uses formed another branch. These milestones establish a commercial production history and its main applications; they do not by themselves establish the first laboratory synthesis of the polymer.
sections.nomenclature: MXD6 and PAMXD6 abbreviate poly(m-xylylene adipamide). MX Nylon is a customary material-family label, but the canonical name specifies the m-xylylene adipamide chemistry.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Poly(m-xylylene adipamide), commonly called MXD6, is the linear polyamide from m-xylylenediamine and adipic acid. A common manufacturing route first prepares an aqueous nylon-salt solution with near-equivalent acid and diamine functionality, then heats it under pressure and removes water while advancing melt polycondensation. Batch examples also add m-xylylenediamine to molten adipic acid under nitrogen, progressively raise temperature, and reduce pressure near the end of reaction; the diamine/diacid balance, water removal, and impurities that form branching species are molecular-mass and end-group controls. Solid-state advancement may be used after melt condensation for a higher-molar-mass resin, but this remains polymer manufacture rather than shaping. The MXD6 homopolymer boundary requires adipic-acid-derived units and m-xylylenediamine-derived units; xylylenediamine copolyamides with terephthalic or other diacids are not substituted for it.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Poly(m-xylylene adipamide) (MXD6) is a crystalline semi-aromatic polyamide, and its measured mechanical response changes with molar mass, crystallization and cooling history, drying/moisture conditioning, temperature, molding versus film orientation, and fillers, plasticizers, or blend partners. Mitsubishi Gas Chemical's MX Nylon table identifies a specific injection-molded MXD6 comparison specimen and reports ASTM D638 tensile strength of 99 MPa, elongation of 2.3%, and tensile modulus of 4.7 GPa; it also reports 3.1% equilibrium moisture uptake at 65% RH, emphasizing that specimen water state should remain explicit. The table does not identify grade, conditioning for the tensile test, geometry, rate, or replicate basis, so these values are not a general MXD6 specification. The same supplier's 15 µm, 4×4 biaxially drawn MXD6 film instead reports ISO 527-3 tensile strengths of 220 MPa in both machine and transverse directions and a 3.8 GPa modulus in both directions, illustrating why oriented-film values cannot be assigned to injection-molded resin. An independent MXD6 composite study further found that plasticizer/nucleator additions changed crystallinity and tensile response, reinforcing the formulation limitation.
sections.processing:
Poly(m-xylylene adipamide) (MXD6) is a melt-processable polyamide used in injection molding and extrusion, including co-injection and coextrusion with PET, polypropylene, polyethylene, or nylon 6 for multilayer containers, bottles, films, sheets, and blow-molded articles; monofilament is another established converted form. Moisture control is important because absorbed water can produce bubbles or silver streaks. Mitsubishi Gas Chemical (MGC) states that its moisture-proof Nylon-MXD6 pellets are supplied at no more than 0.1% water and may be molded directly after opening, while opened material should be kept dry. For moisture-exposed pellets, MGC gives reduced-pressure drying at 120–140 °C for 4–5 h and 0.5–2 mmHg. The same technical record places its Nylon-MXD6 molding range at 250–290 °C and warns against exceeding 300 °C because decomposition can lower viscosity and cause discoloration. These are supplier instructions for MGC's Nylon-MXD6 material, not a universal family window.

As one bounded compounding example, Zhao and co-workers dried MXD6 pellets at 110 °C under vacuum for 12 h and dried their DT flame retardant and P22 nucleant at 80 °C for 12 h. They compounded the specified MXD6/DT/P22 formulations in a 16 mm, L/D 25 co-rotating twin-screw extruder at 30 rpm with zones set to 220/250/250/260/260/260/265/265/265/240 °C, air-cooled and pelletized the strand, then vacuum-dried the compounded pellets at 80 °C for 24 h. Their test pieces were injection molded at 270 °C or hot-pressed at 280 °C and 20 MPa for 5 min. Those settings describe that study's modified formulations and laboratory equipment; they also illustrate why drying, additive mixing, cooling history, and the relatively slow crystallization of neat MXD6 must be managed together.
sections.structureAndMorphology: MXD6 is an aromatic polyamide formed from m-xylylenediamine and adipic acid. Its rigid aromatic-containing repeat units produce a semicrystalline polyamide with hydrogen-bonded amide domains and composition-dependent crystallization.
sections.properties: MXD6 offers high gas-barrier performance, stiffness, strength, and relatively low oxygen permeability, while remaining melt processable as a thermoplastic. Crystallinity, orientation, humidity, molecular mass, and blending influence barrier and dimensional behavior.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. MXD6 is used as a barrier component in packaging films, sheets, bottles, trays and cups, including blends or multilayers with PET, PP or PA6. These uses principally serve food and beverage packaging converters.

Purchasing. Mitsubishi Gas Chemical supplies different molecular-weight grades: S6007 is listed for films, PET bottle blends and monofilaments; S6121 for multilayer sheet and blow-molded bottles/tubes; #6000 for injection moldings. Buyers can request the selected material through the product-inquiry channel.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable separate annual MXD6 purchased or consumed tonnage was established from the checked source. It lists applications and grades without quantifying resin fractions in packages or annual demand.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Repeated melt processing changes MXD6 chain structure. In a thesis studying pure MXD6 alongside PET and their blends, viscosity changes were interpreted as competition between chain scission and branching/crosslinking. This is a rheological interpretation, not a resolved inventory of released molecules.

Timescales: Pure MXD6 was extruded through three recycling cycles. Separate isothermal rheology followed behavior for 1,200 s at 270 °C in air or nitrogen; these are processing and accelerated thermal tests.

Environmental persistence: These experiments do not measure biodegradation, mineralization or disappearance in soil or water. No ambient lifetime is assigned.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: The thesis demonstrates three melt-reprocessing cycles for pure MXD6 at laboratory scale, with structural and rheological changes that constrain reuse. A manufacturer collaboration reports recycling-compatible polypropylene barrier packaging incorporating MXD6 and supported by APR testing. This is compatibility of the specified multilayer packaging with a PP stream, not recovery of pure MXD6 or blanket acceptance of all MXD6-containing articles. An acid-hydrolysis patent also names MXD6, without demonstrating an MXD6 example.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Poly(m-xylylene adipamide) processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: Moisture and thermal history can alter barrier, crystallization, and processing behavior, and high crystallinity can slow molding cycles. Diamine/diacid balance, molecular mass, nucleation, blend compatibility, orientation, humidity, and layer thickness must accompany comparisons between grades.

sections.overview: Polyphthalamides (PPA) are a family of semiaromatic polyamides made from phthalic-acid components and diamines. Published salt and polycondensation routes illustrate that the specific aromatic acid and diamine choices define the particular PPA polymer.
sections.history: Polyphthalamides developed through several semiaromatic polyamide programs, rather than one invention shared by all compositions. A well-documented industrial lineage is Amoco’s Amodel business: development began in the early 1980s, a Greenville semiworks facility followed in 1987, and the first commercial Augusta unit began operating in 1993. Automotive, electronic, consumer and medical-device components became markets. The business passed to Solvay in 2001. Kuraray’s separate 1999 GENESTAR launch illustrates another branch of this family. These histories concern specific commercial compositions and manufacturing programs; they should not be transferred indiscriminately to every PPA or its constituent homopolyamides.
sections.nomenclature: PPA is a family designation, not one fixed nylon composition or a reinforced grade. Terephthalic, isophthalic, and related aromatic-acid components, as well as the selected diamine, distinguish family members; a fiber-reinforced PPA is a separate composite formulation.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyphthalamides are semi-aromatic polyamides in which a substantial fraction of the diacid component is terephthalic acid, isophthalic acid, or another aromatic dicarboxylic acid. These acids are paired with aliphatic or cycloaliphatic diamines such as hexamethylenediamine, nonanediamine, decanediamine, or trimethylhexamethylenediamine. A common manufacturing sequence first forms an approximately equimolar diammonium dicarboxylate nylon salt in water, isolates or concentrates it, and then polycondenses it while removing feed water and condensation water under controlled pressure and temperature; solid-state finishing can raise molar mass without prolonged residence in a very hot melt. Terephthalic/isophthalic ratio, diamine mixture, optional aliphatic diacid or lactam comonomer, stoichiometric offset, and monofunctional chain stopper control melting behavior, sequence, molar mass, and end groups. One cited patent covers preparation and purification of aromatic-diacid nylon salts across multiple diamines. A distinct patent demonstrates pressurized salt conversion and finishing for hexamethylene terephthalamide. Individual PA6T, PA9T, PA10T, and copolyamide records retain route-specific detail.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyphthalamides (PPAs) are semi-aromatic polyamides whose stiffness, strength, ductility, and impact response depend on tere/isophthalamide ratio, crystallinity and moisture, molecular mass, temperature/rate, and especially fiber content, aspect ratio, and flow-induced orientation. An unfilled PPA study measured 3.31 ± 0.09 GPa modulus and 97.72 ± 6.91 MPa ultimate tensile strength at room temperature; 30 wt% short carbon fiber raised these to 12.79 ± 0.56 GPa and 142.72 ± 12.47 MPa. These are the study's particular PPA and fiber composites, not family constants. A separate PPA/PA410 study reports room-temperature brittleness and strain hardening, with temperature altering strain hardening; blends and filled grades must remain distinct.
sections.processing:
Polyphthalamides are high-temperature melt thermoplastics whose principal documented article-conversion route is injection molding of neat, impact-modified, mineral-filled, and short- or long-fiber-reinforced grades. Pellets are hygroscopic and require desiccant drying, dry-air conveying, and sealed handling through the hopper; wet resin can hydrolyze during melting, lower viscosity and molar mass, and cause flash, short shots, dimensional variation, or poor properties. Clean sprues and runners may be reground, but the regrind must be kept identified, contamination-free, size-classified, and dried, and repeated heat histories can reduce viscosity. Because PPA melt temperatures and mold temperatures are high, machine shot capacity, screw compression and recovery, shear heating, nonreturn performance, melt residence time, nozzle control, and a purging plan are important. Reinforced grades can accelerate tool wear and fiber breakage, while gate and runner layout, fill velocity, packing and hold, venting, mold-temperature uniformity, cooling time, and insert preheating govern knit lines, fiber orientation, crystallization, shrinkage, warpage, surface finish, and cracking around inserts. Long hot holds should be avoided and the barrel purged during interruptions to limit degradation. Nylon-salt formation and polycondensation belong in Synthesis; drying, regrind preparation, melt filling, packing, cooling, and demolding of finished resin belong in Processing.

Solvay's Amodel guide gives portfolio-specific starting points rather than a family-wide PPA window. It recommends a desiccant dryer able to maintain about a −30 °C dew point and, in its starting table, 4 h drying at 110 or 120 °C depending on the named Amodel series. The same table gives series-dependent target melt ranges spanning about 320–345 °C; the guide recommends estimated residence no longer than 6 min, warns against holding melt above 350 °C, and advises purging if a molding interruption exceeds 10 min. A separate open experiment by Shen and co-workers provides a bounded molding example for neat N100 PPA and four named 30–50 wt% carbon- or glass-fiber PPA granulates, including Amodel AS-1133 HS. They molded plates on an RR/TSMP laboratory machine at 360 °C cylinder temperature, 150 °C mold temperature, and 9 bar, then CNC-cut specimens from the plates. Those conditions apply only to the reported grades, plate geometry, and laboratory machine and should not be generalized to other PPA chemistries or commercial parts.
sections.structureAndMorphology: Polyphthalamides are semiaromatic polyamides whose aromatic-diacid and diamine selection defines a particular PPA chain composition.
sections.properties: Neat PPA and fiber-reinforced PPA differ strongly in tensile, impact, and orientation-sensitive response; temperature and crystallinity can also change ductility and strain hardening.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PPA grades serve molded engineering parts and metal replacement; heating-system examples include manifolds, heat meters, pumps and valves. Reinforcement, composition and service qualification vary across the family.

Purchasing. Buy a named PPA compound, specifying chemistry and reinforcement. EMS distinguishes PA6T/6I, PA6T/66 and PA10T/X grades; Syensqo markets Amodel grades for heating components.

Scale and evidence limits. The checked supplier catalogs do not provide annual PPA purchased mass or its division among industries. Named nylon-family capacities cannot automatically be summed into a consistent PPA market total.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: The Amodel PPA guide documents thermal degradation during excessive melt residence and changes from repeated processing. Chemical hydrolysis is demonstrated for a named PA66/6T copolyamide in a separate patent; the broad family does not have one product distribution.

Timescales: The patent treats the 35/65 PA66/6T composition under acid reflux for 24 h with a 120 °C oil bath. These are recovery conditions, not an environmental timescale.

Environmental persistence: Neither source establishes mineralization or a family-wide environmental lifetime.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: Mechanical reuse of dry, clean regrind is documented for named Amodel formulations. The guide requires control of contamination, heat history and regrind proportion. Acid hydrolysis is a separate patent-demonstrated route for the specified PA66/6T composition.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyphthalamide family processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: Fiber content, aspect ratio, orientation, polymer composition, temperature, crystallinity, and specimen method constrain every reported PPA property.

sections.overview: Polyamide 6/66 is a copolyamide containing units associated with PA6 and PA66. Copolymer composition changes hydrogen bonding, crystallization, and fiber or molded-material behavior relative to either homopolyamide.
sections.history: PA6/66 copolyamides developed by combining caprolactam-derived and nylon-66-derived units to adjust behavior for particular applications. A documented packaging milestone is Hartmut Grund’s Naturin patent, filed in 1995 and granted in 1997, which identifies PA6/66 in multilayer tubular films for food casings. BASF’s later work on Ultramid C and multilayer-film recycling shows continued development of this packaging role into the 2020s. These records identify useful application milestones, not the original synthesis date of the copolymer. A PA6/66 chain copolymer also has a different history from a physical blend of separate PA6 and PA66 resins.
sections.nomenclature: PA6/66 denotes a PA6–PA66 copolyamide, not a physical blend of PA6 and PA66. The slash convention describes the component polyamide units but does not by itself define a fixed composition.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 6/66 is a copolyamide, not a physical PA 6/PA 66 blend: it contains caprolactam-derived PA 6 units together with PA 66 units made from equimolar hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid (the AH salt). Documented preparations co-charge caprolactam and AH salt, use water to initiate caprolactam ring opening, then heat while removing water so that ring-opened and salt-derived species polycondense into a random or near-random copolyamide. The caprolactam/AH-salt ratio is therefore a composition control; adding another diamine or diacid creates a different copolyamide rather than defining PA 6/66.
sections.mechanicalProperties:
PA6/66 is a hydrogen-bonded, semicrystalline copolyamide whose room-temperature response can range from stiff and yielding when dry to much softer and tougher after moisture uptake. Introducing PA66 repeat units into a PA6 chain disrupts sequence regularity and changes hydrogen-bond organization, crystal form, crystallization, and drawability; the response therefore depends on the 6:66 ratio and sequence distribution, not just the two parent-polyamide property sets. Molar mass and end-group balance, crystalline fraction and morphology, cooling and annealing, fiber draw ratio and heat setting, molding or printing orientation, voids and weld or layer interfaces, specimen thickness, moisture content, test temperature and rate, and glass, mineral, elastomer, or flame-retardant additions all affect modulus, yield, impact, and elongation. A PA6/PA66 physical blend is not automatically equivalent to a random PA6/66 copolyamide and should retain its own morphology and formulation context.

A bounded additive-manufacturing example is Polymaker PolyMide CoPA, identified by its supplier as a nylon 6/nylon 6,6 copolymer filament. For 100%-infill specimens printed at a 260 °C nozzle and 50 °C bed, then annealed at 80 °C for 6 hours and dried for 48 hours, typical ISO 527 X–Y values were 2703 ± 259 MPa Young's modulus, 78.0 ± 0.7 MPa tensile strength, and 12.7 ± 2.1% elongation at break. Dry Z specimens were weaker and less extensible—2209 ± 59 MPa, 45.8 ± 1.5 MPa, and 1.3 ± 0.1%—showing print-direction sensitivity. After the same anneal followed by 48 hours in 60 °C water to an average 6.16% moisture content, X–Y modulus and strength were 724 ± 61 MPa and 34.3 ± 2.5 MPa, while notched Charpy impact rose from the dry 6.9 ± 1.4 to 27.7 ± 1.2 kJ/m². These typical values apply only to that proprietary printed grade, geometry, orientation, and conditioning; the supplier does not disclose copolymer ratio or molar mass.
sections.processing: PA6/66 copolyamide processing depends on the caprolactam/adipamide balance, molecular mass, moisture, and whether the product is a molding resin or a fiber/filament grade. A public fiber study converts composition-series PA6/66 by solution/melt spinning followed by multistep drawing and thermal setting; composition and draw history are part of the reported fiber process, not a universal recipe. A separate Polymaker PA6/66 filament document describes drying, hot-water conditioning, annealing, and fused-filament printing settings for a named commercial filament, demonstrating a second conversion route with explicit moisture and post-treatment controls. Those settings belong to the named filament and printer, while other PA6/66 molding or textile grades require separate drying and thermal-window qualification.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA6/66 is a composition-variable copolyamide combining PA6 and PA66 units.
sections.properties: Hydrogen bonding and crystallization vary with copolymer composition and fiber processing.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA6/66 copolymer grades are used in packaging films, shrink films and monofilaments. BASF’s Ultramid C portfolio assigns these uses to specific grades.

Purchasing. Specify copolyamide PA6/66 rather than a physical PA6/PA66 blend. BASF lists grades by viscosity and additives and provides product-information and commercial ordering channels.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable separate PA6/66 annual purchased or consumed tonnage was established. Broader nylon statistics cannot isolate this copolymer, and a grade listing is not a sales-volume estimate.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: The SAMPE study compares thermal decomposition of neat PA6/66 copolyamide with flame-retarded and nanofilled formulations. It measures mass loss and residual char; individual evolved molecules are not identified.

Timescales: The TGA protocol uses approximately 17–18 mg samples heated in nitrogen at 20 °C/min. Its thermal thresholds cannot be converted into a soil or water lifetime.

Environmental persistence: No environmental mineralization or disappearance time is established in the thermal or film-recycling sources.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: Nurel reports mechanical-recycling compatibility of specified coextruded PE/PA6/66 packaging in a PE film stream, based on cyclos-HTP tests with up to 30% copolyamide. This is a packaging-structure result, not universal collection acceptance or isolation of pure PA6/66.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 6/66 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: The cited high-strength fiber study concerns a specified copolymer and spinning route.

synthesisRoutes.mechanism: Lactam ring opening and salt-derived condensation form a covalent PA6/66 copolyamide. In the water-assisted route, lactam opening generates amino/carboxyl functionality. steps.title: Form and recover the product
steps.body: Open the lactam with water and heat while removing water to advance the copolyamide.
